description: Trees are hierarchical, non-linear data structures consisting of nodes connected by edges. They are acyclic, connected graphs with a single root node. Common types include Binary Trees (max 2 children) and Binary Search Trees (left child < root < right child).
important_details: Traversals: Depth-First Search (DFS) includes Preorder (Root-Left-Right), Inorder (Left-Root-Right), and Postorder (Left-Right-Root). Breadth-First Search (BFS) is Level Order.
Recursive Nature: Most tree problems are naturally solved using recursion because the tree itself is a recursive data structure (a node contains its children).
Base Cases: Always handle the `null` node base case first to avoid NullPointerExceptions.
BST Property: Inorder traversal of a Binary Search Tree yields nodes in strictly ascending order.
other_relevant_details: When solving tree problems, first identify if it is a standard Binary Tree or a BST. If it is a BST, you can often achieve O(H) time complexity (where H is height) by eliminating half of the tree at each step, similar to Binary Search. Watch out for skewed trees (height O(N)) which can cause StackOverflowErrors during deep recursion.

variations.description: Visiting nodes level by level from top to bottom, and left to right within each level. Typically implemented using a Queue.
important_details: Data Structure: Use a Queue (FIFO) to process nodes.
Level Distinction: To process nodes level by level, capture the queue size `int size = queue.size()` in a loop before polling elements.
Useful for finding the maximum width, shortest path in unweighted trees, or level-based aggregations.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(N). Space Complexity: O(W) where W is the maximum width of the tree.

variations.description: A variation of BFS where nodes are traversed left-to-right on even levels and right-to-left on odd levels.
important_details: Use a boolean flag `leftToRight` to track direction.
If `leftToRight` is false, insert elements at the front of the list (index 0) or reverse the list before adding to the result.
Toggle the flag at the end of each level.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(N). Space Complexity: O(W). Using a `LinkedList` for the level allows O(1) insertion at both ends.

variations.description: Finding the nodes visible when viewing the tree strictly from the right or left side.
important_details: BFS Approach: The right side view consists of the last node in each level of a standard BFS.
DFS Approach: Recurse right child first. If `depth == result.size()`, it means it's the first node seen at this depth, so add it to the result.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(N). Space Complexity: O(H) for DFS recursion stack.

problems.name: Left Side View of Binary Tree

variations.description: Finding the nodes visible when viewing the tree strictly from above or below, considering horizontal distances.
important_details: Assign a horizontal distance (hd) to each node. Root is 0. Left child is `hd - 1`. Right child is `hd + 1`.
Use a TreeMap to store the first seen node (Top View) or last seen node (Bottom View) for each `hd`.
BFS is preferred over DFS to ensure top-to-bottom priority is maintained correctly.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(N log N) due to TreeMap. Space: O(N).

variations.description: Grouping nodes by their column index. If multiple nodes are in the same row and column, sort them by value.
important_details: Track `(row, col)` for each node.
Often requires a nested TreeMap: `TreeMap<Integer, TreeMap<Integer, PriorityQueue<Integer>>>` to group by col, then row, then sort by value.
Unlike Top/Bottom view, Vertical Order includes ALL nodes in a column, not just the top/bottom-most.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(N log N) due to TreeMap and PriorityQueues. Space: O(N).

problems.name: Vertical Order Traversal of a Binary Tree

variations.description: Finding the maximum width of the tree, where width is defined as the number of nodes between the leftmost and rightmost non-null nodes in a level.
important_details: Assign a numerical index to each node. Root is 1. Left child is `2 * parent_index`. Right child is `2 * parent_index + 1`.
Width of a level = `rightmost_index - leftmost_index + 1`.
Beware of integer overflow. Use `long` for indices or cast carefully.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(N). Space Complexity: O(W).

variations.description: Finding all nodes at a specific distance K from a target node. Since trees are directed downward, we must convert it to an undirected graph to traverse upwards.
important_details: Step 1: DFS/BFS to build a child-to-parent map (undirected graph representation).
Step 2: Standard BFS starting from the target node.
Use a `visited` set to avoid cycles, as we can now move to parent nodes.

problems.name: All Nodes Distance K in Binary Tree

variations.description: Rebuilding a tree from its traversal arrays (e.g., Preorder + Inorder, Postorder + Inorder).
important_details: Preorder/Postorder gives the root node.
Find the root in the Inorder array to determine the size of the left and right subtrees.
Use a HashMap for O(1) lookups of indices in the Inorder array.
Recursively construct the left and right subtrees by adjusting array boundaries.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(N). Space Complexity: O(N) for map and recursion stack.

variations.description: Calculating the depth, checking balance, or finding the diameter (longest path between any two nodes) of a tree.
important_details: Height is calculated as `1 + max(left_height, right_height)`.
Diameter is the number of edges on the longest path. It can either pass through the root (`left_height + right_height`) or be entirely within the left or right subtree.
Use an instance variable or array to track the max diameter across all recursive calls.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(N). Space Complexity: O(H).

variations.description: Traversing from the root to every leaf, accumulating values, sums, or building path strings. Often involves backtracking.
important_details: A leaf node is identified by `node.left == null && node.right == null`.
Backtracking: Add the current node to the path before recursing, and remove it after the recursive calls return.
Path Sum: Pass the running sum down. If it's a leaf, check if running sum equals target.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(N) to visit nodes, but copying paths can make it O(N^2) in the worst case for output. Space: O(H).

variations.description: Finding the Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA) of two nodes, or finding the Kth ancestor.
important_details: LCA Logic: If current node is p or q, return it. Recurse left and right.
If left and right both return non-null, the current node is the LCA.
If one is null, return the non-null one (LCA is in that subtree).
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(N). Space: O(H). For BST, LCA is simpler: traverse down, if both p,q are smaller go left, if both larger go right, else root is LCA.

variations.description: Operations leveraging the BST property (left < root < right).
important_details: Inorder traversal yields a sorted array. Useful for finding Kth smallest, or fixing swapped nodes.
Search/Insert/Delete operations take O(H) time.
Delete node with 2 children: Find inorder successor (smallest in right subtree), replace value, and delete the successor.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(H) average, O(N) worst case for skewed trees. Space: O(H) for recursion.

variations.description: Problems where the state at a node depends on the states of its children. Solved using Post-order DFS.
important_details: Usually requires returning an array or custom object representing multiple states (e.g., `[rob, not_rob]`).
Post-order is mandatory: solve subproblems (left/right subtrees) before the current node.
Example: House Robber III. If you rob a node, you cannot rob its children. If you don't, you can rob them.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(N). Space Complexity: O(H) for recursion stack.

variations.description: Converting a tree to a string format for storage or transmission, and rebuilding it back.
important_details: Preorder traversal is most common for serialization.
Must explicitly serialize `null` nodes (e.g., as 'X' or '#') to preserve structure.
Deserialization uses a Queue or Iterator to consume the string tokens recursively.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(N) for both. Space Complexity: O(N) for string and recursion stack.

variations.description: Restructuring the tree in place, such as flattening it to a linked list or trimming nodes outside a range.
important_details: Flatten to Linked List: Can be done in O(1) space using Morris Traversal, or simply by Reverse Post-order traversal maintaining a `prev` pointer.
Trim BST: Recursively trim left and right. If current node is out of range, replace it with its left or right child.
variations.other_relevant_details: Time Complexity: O(N). Space Complexity: O(H) for recursion, or O(1) if using iterative Morris traversal.
